en.headline: July consumer prices rise 1.7% year on year as inflation stays moderate
en.dek: The smaller increase from June mainly reflected a rates concession; underlying inflation held at 1.9% after stripping out one-off relief measures.
body: The Census and Statistics Department reported on Thursday that the Composite Consumer Price Index rose 1.7% year on year in July 2026, slower than the 2.0% increase recorded in June.

The smaller rise was mainly attributable to the Government’s rates concession in July 2026, which was not in place in July 2025. Netting out all one-off relief measures, the underlying inflation rate remained at 1.9%, unchanged from June.

Electricity, gas and water recorded the largest increase at 10.8%, followed by transport at 5.0% and miscellaneous services at 4.9%. A government spokesman said overall inflation remained moderate, with price pressures from most components generally under control despite elevated fuel-related costs.

zh.headline: 7月綜合消費物價指數按年升1.7% 基本通脹維持1.9%
zh.dek: 升幅較6月放緩主因差餉寬免，剔除政府一次性措施後基本通脹率與上月相同。
body: 政府統計處周四公布，2026年7月綜合消費物價指數按年上升1.7%，低於6月的2.0%升幅。
較低升幅主要由於7月有差餉寬免而去年同期沒有。剔除所有政府一次性紓困措施後，基本通脹率為1.9%，與6月相同。
電力、燃氣及水升幅最大，達10.8%，其後為交通5.0%及雜項服務4.9%。政府發言人表示整體通脹仍屬溫和，大部分項目價格壓力受控，惟燃料相關項目通脹仍然偏高。
